title: Fourteen Winters and One Short Gate
subtitle: 时间管理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 时间管理（人与自我·生活与学习）
meta: 主题语境：时间管理（人与自我·生活与学习）　|　核心词汇：end　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 end 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1947 my grandmother ① reached an end that no walker in the lane would have named, and she said the reaching was the whole of the winter. The ② end, meaning the tip and not the finish, ran fourteen winters and stayed unnamed in the book; an end, she said, is the only thing in a lane that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ end in that lane had the same short gate beside it, and the ④ end at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the orchard and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An end, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; my grandmother said the naming is the part that fills fourteen winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the end was the whole of the story, meaning the finish and not the tip. The ⑥ end, meaning the finish and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody waits for and nobody names; end, he said, is either something you reach or the only word that means both a tip and a finish. He said the finish is the part they remember.

By 1956 the ⑦ end had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short gate. The ⑧ end of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in January, was one lane and fourteen winters of naming; end, she said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to name. She said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ end I remember is the one named in the plan, which closed in 1968 and is still described as the quietest in the lane. An ⑩ end, my mother said in 1970, is the only one that improves by being named; every end, she said, is a finish that has agreed to look like a tip. She said the finish was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 尽头；末端（指那条小路上走到的那一处）
B. n. 尽头；末端（指那个尽头本身，与结束相对）
C. 固定搭配：reach an end 走到尽头
D. n. 尽头；末端（指留给果园的那一端）
E. n. 尽头；末端（抽象总称，指一条小路的尽头之事）
F. n. 尽头；末端（指图样上写到、被标名的那一端）
G. n. 结束；结局（指故事里人人都等却无人命名的那样东西）
H. n. 结束（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人命名的那种结果）

items.q: reached an end that no walker in the lane would have named
The end, meaning the tip and not the finish
the end at the far side
the end was the whole of the story
the end had become a line in a plan
The end of the whole thing
An end, my mother said in 1970

answers.why: reach an end 意为“走到尽头”，1947 年祖母走到了一处小路上没有一位行人肯说出口的尽头。
end 意为“尽头、末端”，指那个尽头本身而不是结束，它经过了十四个冬天而在簿子上没有名字。
end 意为“尽头、末端”，指那条小路上的每一处尽头，每一处旁边都有同一道短短的栅门。
end 意为“尽头、末端”，指留给果园的那一端，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
end 意为“结束、结局”，指故事里人人都等却无人命名的那样东西，叔叔说这个结局就是那个故事的全部。
end 意为“结束”，指人人都等却无人命名的那种结果而不是那个尽头，是故事里人人都等、却无人命名的东西。
end 意为“尽头、末端”，指图样上写到、被标名的那一端，到 1956 年这一端成了图样里的一行。
end 意为“尽头、末端”，祖母一月写道，整件事的尽头之事是一条小路和十四个冬天的命名。
end 意为“尽头、末端”，我记得的是图样上标名的那一处，1968 年封了，至今仍被说成小路上最安静的一处。
end 为抽象总称，母亲 1970 年说，一处尽头是唯一会因为被好好命名而变得更好的东西。
